full_text: BEFORE THE DEPARTMENT OF WATER RESOURCES OF THE STATE OF IDAHO IN THE MATTER OF A DECLARATION) OF DROUGHT EMERGENCY FOR ) GOODING COUNTY ) _____________ ) ORDER DECLARING DROUGHT EMERGENCY WHEREAS, both the Big Wood River and Little Wood River watersheds in Gooding County are experiencing near record low water supplies this year; and WHEREAS, the Natural Resource Conservation Service's May 1 report indicates that this year's supply for the Snake River is forecast to be the ninth lowest in 50 years with only 11 percent carryover storage at the end of the 2001 water year; and WHEREAS, the Gooding County Commissioners have requested declaration of a drought emergency to allow administrative actions to lessen the severe impacts of the drought conditions in the county; and WHEREAS, section 42-222A, Idaho Code, provides that upon declaration of a drought emergency for an area designated by the Director of the Department of Water Resources ("Director") and approved by the Governor, the Director is authorized to allow temporary changes in the point of diversion, the place of use, and the purpose of use for valid existing water rights and temporary exchanges of water rights when the Director determines that such changes can be accomplished in accordance with the provisions of section 42-222A, Idaho Code; and WHEREAS, the existing Amended Moratorium Order of the Director of the Department of Water Resources, dated April 30, 1993, applicable to the Eastern Snake River Plain Area, including Gooding County, does not prohibit the processing or approval of applications for transfer of existing water rights; NOW, THEREFORE, IT IS HEREBY ORDERED that pursuant to the authority of the Director provided in section 42-222A, Idaho Code, a drought emergency for purposes of section 42-222A, Idaho Code, is hereby declared for Gooding County, Idaho. IT IS FURTHER HEREBY ORDERED that pursuant to this declared drought emergency and the provisions of section 42-222A, Idaho Code, the following procedures and requirements shall apply to the filing, processing, and approval of any application for a temporary change to an existing water right within Gooding County during the pendency of this declared drought emergency: ORDER- Pg 1 1. An application for a temporary change to an existing water right shall be made upon forms provided by the department and shall be accompanied by an application fee of fifty dollars ($50.00) per application. 2. The Director is not required to publish notice of the proposed change pursuant to the provisions of section 42-211, 42-222(1 ), or 42-240, Idaho Code, and is not required to make findings as provided in said sections. A temporary change may be approved upon completion of the application form, payment of the filing fee, and a determination by the Director that the proposed change can be properly administered and there is no information that the change will injure any other water right. If the right to be changed is administered by a watermaster within a water district, the Director shall obtain and consider the recommendations of the watermaster before approving the temporary change application. 3. All temporary changes approved pursuant to the provisions of this order shall expire on the date shown in the approval which shall not be later than December 31, 2002, and thereafter, the water right shall revert to the point of diversion and place of use existing prior to the temporary change. Nothing herein shall be construed as approval to authorize construction of a new well as a new point of diversion or to alter a stream channel. 4. The recipient of an approved temporary change issued pursuant to this order shall assume all risk of curtailment or mitigation should the diversion and use of water under the temporary change cause injury to other water rights or result in an enlargement in use of the original right. 5. Temporary changes shall only be approved for the purpose of providing a replacement water supply to lands or other uses which normally have a full water supply, except for the drought condition. Temporary changes may not be approved to provide water for new development or to allow expansion of the use of water under existing water rights. If the right to use the water, the diversion works of the water delivery system is represented by shares of stock in a corporation, or if the diversion works or delivery system for such right is owned or managed by an irrigation district, no change in point of diversion, place or nature of use of such water shall be made or allowed without the written consent of such corporation or irrigation district. 6. Any applicant for a temporary change who is aggrieved by a denial of the Director for a temporary change pursuant to this order and the provisions of section 42-222A, Idaho Code, may request a hearing pursuant to section 42-1701A(3), Idaho Code, and may seek judicial review of the final order of the Director pursuant to the provisions of section 42- 1701A(4), Idaho Code. full_text: BEFORE THE DEPARTMENT OF WATER RESOURCES OF THE STATE OF IDAHO IN THE MATTER OF A DECLARATION) OF DROUGHT EMERGENCY FOR ) CUSTER COUNTY ) ) ORDER DECLARING DROUGHT EMERGENCY WHEREAS, Custer County is experiencing continued drought conditions that began in 1999 resulting in much of this year's snowpack being absorbed in the soil rather than ending up as streamflow in the Big Lost River; and WHEREAS, the Custer County Commissioners have requested declaration of a drought emergency to allow administrative actions to lessen the severe impacts of the drought conditions in the county; and WHEREAS, section 42-222A, Idaho Code, provides that upon declaration of a drought emergency for an area designated by the Director of the Department of Water Resources ("Director") and approved by the Governor, the Director is authorized to allow temporary changes in the point of diversion, the place of use, and the purpose of use for valid existing water rights and temporary exchanges of water rights when the Director determines that such changes can be accomplished in accordance with the provisions of section 42-222A, Idaho Code; and WHEREAS, the existing Amended Moratorium Order of the Director of the Department of Water Resources, dated April 30, 1993, applicable to the Eastern Snake River Plain Area, including parts of Custer County, and the Amended Moratorium Order of the Director dated April 30, 1993 applicable to the Salmon River drainage does not prohibit the processing or approval of applications for transfer of existing water rights; NOW, THEREFORE, IT IS HEREBY ORDERED that pursuant to the authority of the Director provided in section 42-222A, Idaho Code, a drought emergency for purposes of section 42-222A, Idaho Code, is hereby declared for Custer County, Idaho. IT IS FURTHER HEREBY ORDERED that pursuant to this declared drought emergency and the provisions of section 42-222A, Idaho Code, the following procedures and requirements shall apply to the filing, processing, and approval of any application for a temporary change to an existing water right within Custer County during the pendency of this declared drought emergency: 1. An application for a temporary change to an existing water right shall be made upon forms provided by the department and shall be accompanied by an application fee of fifty dollars ($50.00) per application. ORDER· Pg 1 2. The Director is not required to publish notice of the proposed change pursuant to the provisions of section 42-211, 42-222(1 ), or 42-240, Idaho Code, and is not required to make findings as provided in said sections. A temporary change may be approved upon completion of the application form, payment of the filing fee, and a determination by the Director that the proposed change can be properly administered and there is no information that the change will injure any other water right. If the right to be changed is administered by a watermaster within a water district, the Director shall obtain and consider the recommendations of the watermaster before approving the temporary change application. 3. All temporary changes approved pursuant to the provisions of this order shall expire on the date shown in the approval which shall not be later than December 31, 2003, and thereafter, the water right shall revert to the point of diversion and place of use existing prior to the temporary change. Nothing herein shall be construed as approval to authorize construction of a new well as a new point of diversion. 4. The recipient of an approved temporary change issued pursuant to this order shall assume all risk of curtailment or mitigation should the diversion and use of water under the temporary change cause injury to other water rights, or result in an enlargement in use of the original right. 5. Temporary changes shall only be approved for the purpose of providing a replacement water supply to lands or other uses that normally have a full water supply, except for the drought condition. Temporary changes may not be approved to provide water for new development or to allow expansion of the use of water under existing water rights. If the right to use the water is represented by shares of stock in a corporation, or if the diversion works or delivery system for such right is owned or managed by an irrigation district, no change in point of diversion, place or nature of use of such water shall be made or allowed without the written consent of such corporation or irrigation district. 6. Any applicant for a temporary change who is aggrieved by a denial of the Director for a temporary change pursuant to this order and the provisions of section 42-222A, Idaho Code, may request a hearing pursuant to section 42-1701A(3), Idaho Code, and may seek judicial review of the final order of the Director pursuant to the provisions of section 42- 1701 A(4 ), Idaho Code. ORDER-Pg 2 IT IS FURTHER HEREBY ORDERED that this order is effective upon approval of toe Governor and expires on December 31, 2003, unless extended or terminated by order of the Director. IT IS FURTHER HEREBY ORDERED that pursuant to this declared drought emergency and the provisions of section 42-222A, Idaho Code, the following procedures and requirements shall apply to the filing, processing, and approval of any ORDER- Pg 1 application for a temporary change to an existing water right within Madison County during the pendency of this declared drought emergency: 1. An application for a temporary change to an existing water right shall be made upon forms provided by the department and shall be accompanied by an application fee of fifty dollars ($50.00) per application. 2. The Director is not required to publish notice of the proposed change pursuant to the provisions of section 42-211, 42-222(1) or 42-240, Idaho Code, and is not required to make findings as provided in said sections. A temporary change may be approved upon completion of the application form, payment of the filing fee, and a determination by the Director that the proposed change can be properly administered and there is no information that the change will injure any other water right. If the right to be changed is administered by a watermaster within a water district, the Director shall obtain and consider the recommendations of the watermaster before approving the temporary change application. 3. All temporary changes approved pursuant to the provisions of this order shall expire on the date shown in the approval which shall not be later than December 31, 2003, and thereafter, the water right shall revert to the point of diversion and place of use existing prior to the temporary change. Nothing herein shall be construed as approval to authorize construction of a new well as a new point of diversion or to alter a stream channel. 4. The recipient of an approved temporary change issued pursuant to this order shall assume all risk of curtailment or mitigation should the diversion and use of water under the temporary change cause injury to other water rights or result in an enlargement in use of the original right. 5. Temporary changes shall only be approved for the purpose of providing a replacement water supply to lands or other uses that normally have a full water supply, except for the drought condition. Temporary changes may not be approved to provide water for new development or to allow expansion of the use of water under existing water rights. If the right to use the water is represented by shares of stock in a corporation, or if the diversion works or delivery system for such right is owned or managed by an irrigation district, no change in point of diversion, place or nature of use of such water shall be made or allowed without the written consent of such corporation or irrigation district. 6. Any applicant for a temporary change who is aggrieved by a denial of the Director for a temporary change pursuant to this order and the provisions of section 42-222A, Idaho Code, may request a hearing pursuant to section 42-1701A(3), Idaho Code, and may seek judicial review of the ORDER-Pg 2 final order of the Director pursuant to the provisions of section 42- 1701A(4), Idaho Code. IT IS FURTHER HEREBY ORDERED that this order is effective upon approval of the Governor and expires on December 31, 2003, unless extended or terminated by order of the Director. IT IS FURTHER HEREBY ORDERED that pursuant to this declared drought emergency and the provisions of section 42-222A, Idaho Code, the following procedures and requirements shall apply to the filing, processing, and approval of any application for a temporary change to an existing water right within Jefferson County during the pendency of this declared drought emergency: ORDER-Pg 1 1. An application for a temporary change to an existing water right shall be made upon forms provided by the department and shall be accompanied by an application fee of fifty dollars ($50.00) per application. 2. The Director is not required to publish notice of the proposed change pursuant to the provisions of section 42-211, 42-222(1) or 42-240, Idaho Code, and is not required to make findings as provided in said sections. A temporary change may be approved upon completion of the application form, payment of the filing fee, and a determination by the Director that the proposed change can be properly administered and there is no information that the change will injure any other water right. If the right to be changed is administered by a watermaster within a water district, the Director shall obtain and consider the recommendations of the watermaster before approving the temporary change application. 3. All temporary changes approved pursuant to the provisions of this order shall expire on the date shown in the approval which shall not be later than December 31, 2004, and thereafter, the water right shall revert to the point of diversion and place of use existing prior to the temporary change. Nothing herein shall be construed as approval to authorize construction of a new well as a new point of diversion or to alter a stream channel. 4. The recipient of an approved temporary change issued pursuant to this order shall assume all risk of curtailment or mitigation should the diversion and use of water under the temporary change cause injury to other water rights or result in an enlargement in use of the original right. 5. Temporary changes shall only be approved for the purpose of providing a replacement water supply to lands or other uses that normally have a full water supply, except for the drought condition. Temporary changes may not be approved to provide water for new development or to allow expansion of the use of water under existing water rights. If the right to use the water is represented by shares of stock in a corporation, or if the diversion works or delivery system for such right is owned or managed by an irrigation district, no change in point of diversion, place or nature of use of such water shall be made or allowed without the written consent of such corporation or irrigation district. 6. Any applicant for a temporary change who is aggrieved by a denial of the Director for a temporary change pursuant to this order and the provisions of section 42- 222A, Idaho Code, may request a hearing pursuant to section 42-l 701A(3), Idaho Code, and may seek judicial review of the final order of the Director pursuant to the provisions of section 42-l 701A(4), Idaho Code. ORDER-Pg2 IT IS FURTHER HEREBY ORDERED that this order is effective upon approval of the Governor and expires on December 31, 2004, unless extended or terminated by order of the Director. ORDER DECLARING DROUGHT EMERGENCY WHEREAS, irrigators in Bear Lake County primarily rely on stream flows in the Bear River, storage water in the Bear Lake, and ground water for water supplies; and WHEREAS, Bear Lake County is experiencing extreme to exceptionally restricted water supplies available for the current irrigation season; and WHEREAS, the April through July 2004 inflow to Bear Lake was only 22 percent of average; and WHEREAS, the Bear River Compact Commission declared a water emergency above Stewart Dam (above Bear Lake) on April 23, 2004, to allocate the limited flow of water in Bear River between water users in Wyoming and Idaho; and WHEREAS, Bear Lake has been drawn down to historic low levels and downstream irrigators will receive less than 40 percent of their normal allotment of storage water; and WHEREAS, the Bear Lake County Commissioners have requested declaration of a drought emergency to allow administrative actions to lessen the severe impacts of the drought conditions in the county; and WHEREAS, section 42-222A, Idaho Code, provides that upon declaration of a drought emergency for an area designated by the Director of the Department of Water Resources ("Director") and approved by the Governor, the Director is authorized to allow temporary changes in the point of diversion, the place of use, and the purpose of use for valid existing water rights and temporary exchanges of water rights when the Director determines that such changes can be accomplished in accordance with the provisions of section 42-222A, Idaho Code; and NOW, THEREFORE, IT IS HEREBY ORDERED that pursuant to the authority of the Director provided in section 42-222A, Idaho Code, a drought emergency for purposes of section 42-222A, Idaho Code, is hereby declared for Bear Lake County, Idaho. ORDER-Pgl IT IS FURTHER HEREBY ORDERED that pursuant to this declared drought emergency and the provisions of section 42-222A, Idaho Code, the following procedures and requirements shall apply to the filing, processing, and approval of any application for a temporary change to an existing water right within Bear Lake County during the pendency of this declared drought emergency: 1. An application for a temporary change to an existing water right shall be made upon forms provided by the department and shall be accompanied by an application fee of fifty dollars ($50.00) per application. 2. The Director is not required to publish notice of the proposed change pursuant to the provisions of section 42-211, 42-222(1) or 42-240, Idaho Code, and is not required to make findings as provided in said sections. A temporary change may be approved upon completion of the application form, payment of the filing fee, and a determination by the Director that the proposed change can be properly administered and there is no information that the change will injure any other water right. If the right to be changed is administered by a watermaster within a water district, the Director shall obtain and consider the recommendations of the watermaster before approving the temporary change application. 3. All temporary changes approved pursuant to the provisions of this order shall expire on the date shown in the approval which shall not be later than December 31, 2004, and thereafter, the water right shall revert to the point of diversion and place of use existing prior to the temporary change. Nothing herein shall be construed as approval to authorize construction of a new well as a new point of diversion or to alter a stream channel. 4. The recipient of an approved temporary change issued pursuant to this order shall assume all risk of curtailment or mitigation should the diversion and use of water under the temporary change cause injury to other water rights or result in an enlargement in use of the original right. 5. Temporary changes shall only be approved for the purpose of providing a replacement water supply to lands or other uses that normally have a full water supply, except for the drought condition. Temporary changes may not be approved to provide water for new development or to allow expansion of the use of water under existing water rights. If the right to use the water is represented by shares of stock in a corporation, or if the diversion works or delivery system for such right is owned or managed by an irrigation district, no change in point of diversion, place or nature of use of such water shall be made or allowed without the written consent of such corporation or irrigation district. 6. Any applicant for a temporary change who is aggrieved by a denial of the Director for a temporary change pursuant to this order and the provisions of section 42- 222A, Idaho Code, may request a hearing pursuant to section 42-l 701A(3), Idaho ORDER-Pg2 Code, and may seek judicial review of the final order of the Director pursuant to the provisions of section 42-701A(4), Idaho Code. IT IS FURTHER HEREBY ORDERED that this order is effective upon approval of the Governor and expires on December 31, 2004, unless extended or terminated by order of the Director. and WHEREAS, Twin Falls County is experiencing severely restricted streamflows from the Snake River and the Salmon Falls Tract for the current irrigation season; and WHEREAS, the steamflow forecast for the Snake River near Heise from April through September is expected to be only 61 percent of normal; and WHEREAS, the April I forecast for the NRCS Surface Water Supply Index (SWSI) for the Snake River system which combines streamflows with reservoir storage carryover predicts a total supply shortfall of over one million acre feet; and WHEREAS, the Salmon Falls Reservoir total supply as of April I is only 16 percent of capacity for 2005, and is expected to only provide about 65 percent of adequate water supply; and WHEREAS, section 42-222A, Idaho Code, provides that upon declaration of a drought emergency for an area designated by the Director of the Department of Water Resources ("Director") and approved by the Governor, the Director is authorized to allow temporary changes in the point of diversion, the place of use, and the purpose of use for valid existing water rights and temporary exchanges of water rights when the Director determines that such changes can be accomplished in accordance with the provisions of section 42-222A, Idaho Code; and NOW, THEREFORE, IT IS HEREBY ORDERED that pursuant to the authority of the Director provided in section 42-222A, Idaho Code, a drought emergency for purposes of section 42-222A, Idaho Code, is hereby declared for Twin Falls County, Idaho. IT IS FURTHER HEREBY ORDERED that pursuant to this declared drought emergency and the provisions of section 42-222A, Idaho Code, the following procedures and requirements shall apply to the filing, processing, and approval of any ORDER-Pg I application for a temporary change to an existing water right within Twin Falls County during the pendency of this declared drought emergency: 1. An application for a temporary change to an existing water right shall be made upon forms provided by the department and shall be accompanied by an application fee of fifty dollars ($50.00) per application. 2. The Director is not required to publish notice of the proposed change pursuant to the provisions of section 42-211, 42-222(1) or 42-240, Idaho Code, and is not required to make findings as provided in said sections. A temporary change may be approved upon completion of the application form, payment of the filing fee, and a determination by the Director that the proposed change can be properly administered and there is no information that the change will injure any other water right. If the right to be changed is administered by a watermaster within a water district, the Director shall obtain and consider the recommendations of the watermaster before approving the temporary change application. 3. All temporary changes approved pursuant to the provisions of this order shall expire on the date shown in the approval which shall not be later than December 31, 2005, and thereafter, the water right shall revert to the point of diversion and place of use existing prior to the temporary change. The recipient of an approved temporary change issued pursuant to this order shall assume all risk of curtailment or mitigation should the diversion and use of water under the temporary change cause injury to other water rights or result in an enlargement in use of the original right. 5. full_text: 0 0 BEFORE THE DEPARTMENT OF WATER RESOURCES OF THE STATE OF IDAHO IN THE MATTER OF ADECLARATION) OF DROUGHT EMERGENCY FOR ) CUSTER COUNTY ) ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~.) ORDER DECLARING DROUGHT EMERGENCY WHEREAS, the Custer County Board of Commissioners have requested that the Governor and the Director of the Idaho Department of Water Resources declare a drought emergency for Custer County to allow administrative actions to lessen the severe impacts of the drought conditions in the county; and WHEREAS, Custer County includes parts of the Salmon and Big Lost River drainages; and WHEREAS, the Big Lost River Basin has experienced below normal snowpack with earlier than normal runoff. The spring precipitation was also below normal, which has resulted in an inadequate water supply; and WHEREAS, overall the Salmon River Basin is expected to have a near normal water year. However, some of the individual snotel data collection sites located in Custer County are below normal for this time of year. Winter precipitation was near normal while spring and summer precipitation has been below normal; and WHEREAS, the Mackey Reservoir is presently at 69 percent of capacity. The low storage volume will affect water deliveries and will impact the economy of the county; and WHEREAS, Section 42-222A, Idaho Code, provides that upon declaration of a drought emergency for an area designated by the Director of the Department of Water Resources ("Director") and approved by the Governor, the Director is authorized to allow temporary changes in the point of diversion, the place of use, and the purpose of use for valid existing water rights and temporary exchanges of water rights when the Director determines that such changes can be accomplished in accordance with the provisions of section 42-222A, Idaho Code. WHEREAS, the existing Amended Moratorium Order of the Director of the Department of Water Resources, dated April 30, 1993, applicable to the Eastern Snake River Plain Area, including parts of Custer County, does not prohibit the processing or approval of applications for transfer of existing water rights. ORDER DECLARING DROUGHT EMERGENCY- Page 1 0 0 NOW, THEREFORE, IT IS HEREBY ORDERED that pursuant to the authority of the Director provided in section 42-222A, Idaho Code, a drought emergency for purposes of section 42-222A, Idaho Code, is hereby declared for Custer County, Idaho. IT IS FURTHER HEREBY ORDERED that pursuant to this declared drought emergency and the provisions of section 42-222A, Idaho Code, the following procedures and requirements shall apply to the filing, processing, and approval of any application for a temporary change to an existing water right within Custer County during the pendency of this declared drought emergency: 1. An application for a temporary change to an existing water right shall be made upon forms provided by the department and shall be accompanied by an application fee of fifty dollars ($50.00) per application. 2. The Director is not required to publish notice of the proposed change pursuant to the provisions of section 42-211, 42-222(1), or 42-240, Idaho Code, and is not required to make findings as provided in said sections. A temporary change may be approved upon completion of the application form, payment of the filing fee, and a determination by the Director that the proposed change can be properly administered and there is no information that the change will injure any other water right. If the right to be changed is administered by a watermaster within a water district, the Director shall obtain and consider the recommendations of the watermaster before approving the temporary change application. 3. All temporary changes approved pursuant to the provisions of this order shall expire on the date shown in the approval which shall not be later than December 31, 2008, and thereafter, the water right shall revert to the point of diversion and place of use existing prior to the temporary change. Nothing herein shall be construed as approval to authorize construction of a new well as a new point of diversion. 4. The recipient of an approved temporary change issued pursuant to this order shall assume all risk of curtailment or mitigation should the diversion and use of water under the temporary change cause injury to other water rights, or result in an enlargement in use of the original right. 5. Temporary changes shall only be approved for the purpose of providing a replacement water supply to lands or other uses that normally have a full water supply, except for the drought condition. Temporary changes may not be approved to provide water for new development or to allow expansion of the use of water under existing water rights. If the right to use the water is represented by shares of stock in a corporation, or if the diversion works or delivery system for such right is owned or managed by an irrigation district, no change in point of diversion, place or nature of use of such water shall be made or allowed without the written consent of such corporation or irrigation district. ORDER DECLARING DROUGHT EMERGENCY- Page 2 0 0 6. Any applicant for a temporary change who is aggrieved by a denial of the Director for a temporary change pursuant to this order and the provisions of section 42- 222A, Idaho Code, may request a hearing pursuant to section 42-1701A(3), Idaho Code, and may seek judicial review of the final order of the Director pursuant to the provisions of section 42-1701A( 4), Idaho Code. According to Section 42-222A, Idaho Code, which provides that upon declaration of a drought emergency for an area designated by the Director of the Department of Water Resources ("Director") and approved by the Governor, the Director is authorized to allow temporary changes in the point of diversion, the place of use, and the purpose of use for valid existing water rights and temporary exchanges of water rights when the Director determines that such changes can be accomplished in accordance with the provisions of section 42-222A, Idaho Code; and The existing Amended Moratorium Order of the Director of the Department of Water Resources, dated April 30, 1993, applicable to the Eastern Snake River Plain Area, including Butte County, does not prohibit the processing or approval of applications for transfer of existing water rights; ORDER DECLARING DROUGHT EMERGENCY - Pg 1 NOW, THEREFORE, IT IS HEREBY ORDERED that pursuant to the authority of the Director provided in section 42-222A, Idaho Code, a drought emergency for purposes of section 42-222A, Idaho Code, is hereby declared for Butte County, Idaho. IT IS FURTHER ORDERED that pursuant to this declared drought emergency and the provisions of section 42-222A, Idaho Code, the following procedures and requirements shall apply to the filing, processing, and approval of any application for a temporary change to an existing water right within Butte County during the pendency of this declared drought emergency: I. An application for a temporary change to an existing water right shall be made upon forms provided by the department and shall be accompanied by an application fee of fifty dollars ($50.00) per application. 2. The Director is not required to publish notice of the proposed change pursuant to the provisions of section 42-211, 42-222(1), or 42-240, Idaho Code, and is not required to make findings as provided in said sections. A temporary change may be approved upon completion of the application form, payment of the filing fee, and a determination by the Director that the proposed change can be properly administered and there is no information that the change will injure any other water right. If the right to be changed is administered by a watermaster within a water district, the Director shall obtain and consider the recommendations of the watermaster before approving the temporary change application. 3. All temporary changes approved pursuant to the provisions of this order shall expire on the date shown in the approval, which shall not be later than December 31, 2008, and thereafter, the water right shall revert to the point of diversion and place of use existing prior to the temporary change. Nothing herein shall be construed as approval to authorize construction of a new well as a new point of diversion. 4. The recipient of an approved temporary change issued pursuant to this order shall assume all risk of curtailment or mitigation should the diversion and use of water under the temporary change cause injury to other water rights, or result in an enlargement in use of the original right. 5. Temporary changes shall only be approved for the purpose of providing a replacement water supply to lands or other uses that normally have a full water supply, except for the drought condition. Temporary changes may not be approved to provide water for new development or to allow expansion of the use of water under existing water rights. If the right to use the water is represented by shares of stock in a corporation, or if the diversion works or delivery system for such right is owned or managed by an irrigation district, no change in point of diversion, place or nature of use of such water shall be made or allowed without the written consent of such corporation or irrigation district. ORDER DECLARING DROUGHT EMERGENCY - Pg 2 • 6. Any applicant for a temporary change who is aggrieved by a denial of the Director for a temporary change pursuant to this order and the provisions of section 42- 222A, Idaho Code, may request a hearing pursuant to section 42-l 701A(3), Idaho Code, and may seek judicial review of the final order of the Director pursuant to the provisions of section 42-l 701A( 4), Idaho Code. IT IS FURTHER HEREBY ORDERED that this order is effective upon approval of the Governor and expires on December 31, 2008, unless extended or terminated by order of the Director. rt. full_text: Spring Flooding Declaration Posted on June 8, 2010 | updated: December 7, 2018 Idaho Bureau of Homeland Security News Release For immediate release, June 8, 2010 Contact: (primary) Robert Feeley, (208) 859-6943 or (secondary) Col. Tim Marsano (208) 407-8838 Idaho Counties under State Disaster Declaration Due to Flooding (Boise) Due to severe weather and flooding conditions in central Idaho, State Senate President Pro Tem and Acting Governor Bob Geddes today declared a disaster emergency in support of Adams, Idaho and Valley counties. With his signature, Senator Geddes paved the way to make state government support available for use in the affected counties. State support could include personnel, equipment and facilities to help the counties deal with the threats to public safety and property. Senator Geddes is Acting Governor while both Governor C.L. “Butch” Otter and Lieutenant Governor Brad Little are out of the state. “Adams, Idaho and Valley county officials have gone above and beyond in their efforts to deal with this unexpected event, and I applaud their work,” Senator Geddes said. “They have now asked for additional help from the State of Idaho, and by signing this declaration I will ensure they get the assistance they need to get through this emergency.” The Disaster Declaration gives the Idaho Bureau of Homeland Security (BHS) authority to assign missions to State of Idaho departments and agencies. The bureau will work closely with the counties to conduct damage assessments and to determine the best methods and sources for handling the emergency. “Idaho is prepared for disasters and assisting Adams, Idaho and Valley Counties in handling situations like this are well within the ability of Idaho state government,” said BHS Director Brigadier General Bill Shawver. “The Idaho Bureau of Homeland Security will work to direct available resources to the task at hand.” At this time the counties are working closely with the BHS Area Field Officers and Idaho Emergency Operations Center to assess the damage caused by the recent flooding. The Idaho Military Division is currently conducting an aerial survey to assist in these damage assessments. Once a clearer picture emerges and the level of damage is apparent, BHS will work with the affected counties to determine how to best allocate resources in the response and recovery to the flooding event. # # # Note to reporters: The Idaho Bureau of Homeland Security is the State of Idaho’s emergency management agency. Please note that Idaho BHS is an Idaho-specific agency, and it is not the same thing as the federal Department of Homeland Security. Within the State of Idaho organizational chart, Idaho BHS is aligned under the State of Idaho Military Division. Original Release Posted in Press Releases

full_text: BEFORE THE DEPARTMENT OF WATER RESOURCES OF THE STATE OF IDAHO IN THE MATTER OF A DECLARATION ) OF DROUGHT EMERGENCY FOR ) BLAINE COUNTY ) ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~-) ORDER DECLARING DROUGHT EMERGENCY WHEREAS, the Board of County Commissioners for Blaine County has requested that the Governor and the Director of the Idaho Department of Water Resources declare a drought emergency for Blaine County to allow administrative actions to lessen the impacts of drought conditions in the county; and WHEREAS, Blaine County is included within the Big Wood River and Little Wood River drainages; and WHEREAS, drainages in and around Blaine County are experiencing abnormally dry conditions with the year's snow packs having melted out about a month early and snow water equivalent levels were below normal in portions of the drainages, particularly areas within the Little Wood basin, including the Fish Creek drainage. The United States Drought Monitor Index shows Blaine County included within that potion of Southern Idaho classified as abnormally dry. Additionally, stream levels and flows are currently running from 20 to 70 percent of normal and local water district watermasters are reporting that water right priority cuts are well ahead of schedule, confirming high water demand due to high temperatures and lack of precipitation over the past one to two months; and WHEREAS, section 42-222A, Idaho Code, provides that upon declaration of a drought emergency for an area designated by the Director of the Department of Water Resources ("Director") and approved by the Governor, the Director is authorized to allow temporary changes in the point of diversion, the place of use, and the purpose of use for valid existing water rights and temporary exchanges of water rights when the Director determines that such changes can be accomplished in accordance with the provisions of section 42-222A, Idaho Code; and NOW, THEREFORE, IT IS HEREBY ORDERED that pursuant to the authority of the Director provided in section 42-222A, Idaho Code, a drought emergency for purposes of section 42-222A, Idaho Code, is hereby declared for Blaine County, Idaho. IT IS FURTHER HEREBY ORDERED that pursuant to this declared drought emergency and the provisions of section 42-222A, Idaho Code, the following procedures and requirements shall apply to the filing, processing, and approval of any application for a temporary change to an existing water right within Blaine County during the pendency of this declared drought emergency: ORDER· Pg 1 ( l . An application for a temporary change to an existing water right shall be made upon forms provided by the department and shall be accompanied by an application fee of fifty dollars ($50.00) per application. 2. The Director is not required to publish notice of the proposed change pursuant to the provisions of section 42-211, 42-222(1) or 42-240, Idaho Code, and is not required to make findings as provided in said sections. A temporary change may be approved upon completion of the application form, payment of the filing fee, and a determination by the Director that the proposed change can be properly administered and there is no information that the change will injure any other water right. If the right to be changed is administered by a watermaster within a water district, the Director shall obtain and consider the recommendations of the watermaster before approving the temporary change application. 3. All temporary changes approved pursuant to the provisions of this order shall expire on the date shown in the approval which shall not be later than December 31, 2012, and thereafter, the water right shall revert to the point of diversion and place of use existing prior to the temporary change. Nothing herein shall be construed as approval to authorize construction of a new well as a new point of diversion or to alter a stream channel. 4. The recipient of an approved temporary change issued pursuant to this order shall assume all risk of curtailment or mitigation should the diversion and use of water under the temporary change cause injury to other water rights or result in an enlargement in use of the original right. 5. Temporary changes shall only be approved for the purpose of providing a replacement water supply to lands or other uses that normally have a full water supply, except for the drought condition. Temporary changes may not be approved to provide water for new development or to allow expansion of the use of water under existing water rights. If the right to use the water is represented by shares of stock in a corporation, or if the diversion works or delivery system for such right is owned or managed by an irrigation district, no change in point of diversion, place or nature of use of such water shall be made or allowed without the written consent of such corporation or irrigation district. 6. Any applicant for a temporary change who is aggrieved by a denial of the Director for a temporary change pursuant to this order and the provisions of section 42- 222A, Idaho Code, may request a hearing pursuant to section 42-1701A(3), Idaho Code, and may seek judicial review of the final order of the Director pursuant to the provisions of section 42-1701A(4), Idaho Code. Box 83720, Boise, Idaho 83720-0098 Phone: (208) 287-4800 FAX: (208) 287-6700 www.idwr.idaho.gov MEMO To: Jeff Peppersack From: Tim Luke 1/)­ Date: July 12, 2012 Subject: Hydrologic data for Big and Little Wood River Basins in Blaine County - Blaine County Drought Declaration This memo summarizes hydrologic conditions in the Big and Little Wood River drainages, and is prepared in response to a request for drought emergency declaration from the Blaine County Commission dated July 3, 2012 (IDWR did not receive a copy of the letter request until July 10). Blaine County includes the upper Big Wood River Basin above magic Reservoir (excluding Camas Creek drainage), and the upper Little Wood River Basin above the confluence of Silver Creek and the Little Wood River. Blaine County also extends into a small portion of the upper Salmon River from Galena Summit to its confluence with Pole and Beaver Creeks, plus Alturas Lake Creek. Water supply and drought conditions currently vary somewhat between the Big and Little Wood River basins. Current reservoir levels and year to date precipitation totals within the two drainages actually meet or slightly exceed average historical levels. The April 2012 snowpack for the Big Wood basin was 94 percent of average but only 81 percent of average for the Little Wood basin. April snowpack for the Fish Creek drainage, a tributary to the Little Wood, was only 73 percent of normal. Although early irrigation season conditions appeared favorable in portions of both basins, a quick snowmelt (a month early in most snow marker locations) coupled with high temperatures and little or no precipitation in late June and early July has resulted in lower than normal stream flow conditions and acceleration of water right priority cuts in water districts in both basins. For example, the stream flow on the Big Wood River at Hailey on July 12, 2012 was about 200 cfs below normal flow for that date (71 percent of average). The Big Wood River near Stanton Crossing above Magic Reservoir on July 12 was only 20 percent of normal. The Little Wood River above High Five Creek near Carey (above Little Wood Reservoir) on July 12 was about 53 percent of normal flow. Additionally, the watermaster for the Big and Little Wood Rivers water districts has reported that water right priority cuts are currently about three weeks ahead of schedule. The Fish Creek watermaster reported very hot and dry conditions with water right priority cuts well ahead of schedule and the limited storage supply expected to be gone in about ten days. The Fish Creek watermaster expects that he will begin curtailing and pro-rating the most senior priority rights when the storage supply runs out. Finally, according to the USDA Drought Monitor, the southeast and south central portion of Idaho is affected by abnormally dry conditions. full_text: BEFORE THE DEPARTMENT OF WATER RESOURCES OF THE STATE OF IDAHO IN THE MATTER OF A DECLARATION ) OF DROUGHT EMERGENCY FOR ) TETON COUNTY ) ORDER DECLARING DROUGHT EMERGENCY WHEREAS, the Board of County Commissioners for Teton County has requested that the Governor and the Director of the Idaho Department of Water Resources declare a drought emergency for Teton County to allow administrative actions to lessen the impacts of drought conditions in the county; and WHEREAS, Teton County is included within the Teton River drainage; and WHEREAS, drainages in and around Teton County are experiencing abnormally dry conditions with the year's snow packs having melted out about a month early and snow water equivalent levels below normal during the late spring season. The United States Drought Monitor Index shows Teton County included within that potion of southern and eastern Idaho classified as abnormally dry. Additionally, stream levels and flows on the Teton River are currently running about 65 percent of normal; there has been a lack of precipitation over the past one to two months (June precipitation at Driggs was 23 percent of normal); and daily temperatures have been up to ten degrees above normal over the past month. Water supply in Teton County will likely be stretched for the remaining irrigation season due to the early snow melt out, reduced stream flow levels, lower than normal summer precipitation, and lack of storage water facilities in the area; and WHEREAS, section 42-222A, Idaho Code, provides that upon declaration of a drought emergency for an area designated by the Director of the Department of Water Resources ("Director") and approved by the Governor, the Director is authorized to allow temporary changes in the point of diversion, the place of use, and the purpose of use for valid existing water rights and temporary exchanges of water rights when the Director determines that such changes can be accomplished in accordance with the provisions of section 42-222A, Idaho Code; and NOW, THEREFORE, IT IS HEREBY ORDERED that pursuant to the authority of the Director provided in section 42-222A, Idaho Code, a drought emergency for purposes of section 42-222A, Idaho Code, is hereby declared for Teton County, Idaho. IT IS FURTHER HEREBY ORDERED that pursuant to this declared drought emergency and the provisions of section 42-222A, Idaho Code, the following procedures and requirements shall apply to the filing, processing, and approval of any application for a temporary change to an existing water right within Teton County during the pendency of this declared drought ORDER-Pg 1 emergency: 1. An application for a temporary change to an existing water right shall be made upon forms provided by the department and shall be accompanied by an application fee of fifty dollars ($50.00) per application. 2. The Director is not required to publish notice of the proposed change pursuant to the provisions of section 42-211, 42-222(1) or 42-240, Idaho Code, and is not required to make findings as provided in said sections. A temporary change may be approved upon completion of the application form, payment of the filing fee, and a determination by the Director that the proposed change can be properly administered and there is no information that the change will injure any other water right. If the right to be changed is administered by a watermaster within a water district, the Director shall obtain and consider the recommendations of the watermaster before approving the temporary change application. 3. All temporary changes approved pursuant to the provisions of this order shall expire on the date shown in the approval which shall not be later than December 31, 2012, and thereafter, the water right shall revert to the point of di version and place of use existing prior to the temporary change. Nothing herein shall be construed as approval to authorize construction of a new well as a new point of diversion or to alter a stream channel. 4. The recipient of an approved temporary change issued pursuant to this order shall assume all risk of curtailment or mitigation should the diversion and use of water under the temporary change cause injury to other water rights or result in an enlargement in use of the original right. 5. Temporary changes shall only be approved for the purpose of providing a replacement water supply to lands or other uses that normally have a full water supply, except for the drought condition. Temporary changes may not be approved to provide water for new development or to allow expansion of the use of water under existing water rights. If the right to use the water is represented by shares of stock in a corporation, or if the diversion works or delivery system for such right is owned or managed by an irrigation district, no change in point of diversion, place or nature of use of such water shall be made or allowed without the written consent of such corporation or irrigation district. 6. Any applicant for a temporary change who is aggrieved by a denial of the Director for a temporary change pursuant to this order and the provisions of section 42- 222A, Idaho Code, may request a hearing pursuant to section 42-l 701A(3), Idaho Code, and may seek judicial review of the final order of the Director pursuant to the provisions of section 42-l 701A(4), Idaho Code. The early snowmelt and higher than normal temperatures during July and August has contributed to more limited water supplies and earlier water delivery curtailments. Current stream flows and levels within Bannock County further indicate reduced water supply in response to recent high temperatures and dry conditions. Average discharge of the Portneuf River at Pocatello for August 7, 2012 is about 30 cfs, which is about 36 percent of normal or 53 cfs below average for this date. Several other gage stations further upstream in the basin are reporting discharge levels slightly below average. However, several local water district watermasters have reported making water right delivery cuts earlier with conditions similar to other drought years. Water supply in Bannock County will likely be stretched for the remaining irrigation season due to the early snow melt out, reduced stream flow levels, and limited storage water facilities in the area. ORDER DECLARING DROUGHT EMERGENCY WHEREAS, the Board of County Commissioners for Lemhi County has requested that the Governor and the Director of the Idaho Department of Water Resources declare a drought emergency for Lemhi County to allow administrative actions to lessen the impacts of drought conditions in the county; and WHEREAS, Lemhi County is located within the Lemhi and Salmon River basins; and WHEREAS, the United States Drought Monitor shows most of Lemhi County is considered abnormally dry; and WHEREAS, the river basins in Lemhi County are experiencing abnormally dry conditions with the year's snow water and precipitation levels being well below normal. Specifically, the Moonshine SNOTEL station, located within Lemhi County and the Lemhi River basin, showed that the snow water equivalent was well below normal and snow melted approximately one month earlier than normal. Similar trends were seen at the other SNOTEL sites within the basins. Current stream flows within the county are below normal. The flows in the Lemhi River at Lemhi have been below the median since the beginning of June. Flows in the Salmon River at Salmon have been below the median flow since mid-July. WHEREAS, section 42-222A, Idaho Code, provides that upon declaration of a drought emergency for an area designated by the Director of the Department of Water Resources ("Director") and approved by the Governor, the Director is authorized to allow temporary changes in the point of diversion, the place of use, and the purpose of use for valid existing water rights and temporary exchanges of water rights when the Director determines that such changes can be accomplished in accordance with the provisions of section 42-222A, Idaho Code; and NOW, THEREFORE, IT IS HEREBY ORDERED that pursuant to the authority of the Director provided in section 42-222A, Idaho Code, a drought emergency for purposes of section 42-222A, Idaho Code, is hereby declared for Lemhi County, Idaho. IT IS FURTHER HEREBY ORDERED that pursuant to this declared drought emergency and the provisions of section 42-222A, Idaho Code, the following procedures and requirements shall apply to the filing, processing, and approval of any application for a temporary change to an existing water right within Lemhi County during the pendency of this declared drought emergency: ORDER-Pg 1 existing water right within Lemhi County during the pendency of this declared drought emergency: 1. An application for a temporary change to an existing water right shall be made upon forms provided by the department and shall be accompanied by an application fee of fifty dollars ($50.00) per application. 2. The Director is not required to publish notice of the proposed change pursuant to the provisions of section 42-211, 42-222( 1) or 42-240, Idaho Code, and is not required to make findings as provided in said sections. A temporary change may be approved upon completion of the application form, payment of the filing fee, and a determination by the Director that the proposed change can be properly administered and there is no information that the change will injure any other water right. If the right to be changed is administered by a watermaster within a water district, the Director shall obtain and consider the recommendations of the watermaster before approving the temporary change application. 3. All temporary changes approved pursuant to the provisions of this order shall expire on the date shown in the approval which shall not be later than December 31, 2012, and thereafter, the water right shall revert to the point of diversion and place of use existing prior to the temporary change. Nothing herein shall be construed as approval to authorize construction of a new well as a new point of diversion or to alter a stream channel. 4. The recipient of an approved temporary change issued pursuant to this order shall assume all risk of curtailment or mitigation should the diversion and use of water under the temporary change cause injury to other water rights or result in an enlargement in use of the original right. 5. Temporary changes shall only be approved for the purpose of providing a replacement water supply to lands or other uses that normally have a full water supply, except for the drought condition. Temporary changes may not be approved to provide water for new development or to allow expansion of the use of water under existing water rights. If the right to use the water is represented by shares of stock in a corporation, or if the diversion works or delivery system for such right is owned or managed by an irrigation district, no change in point of diversion, place or nature of use of such water shall be made or allowed without the written consent of such corporation or irrigation district. 6. Any applicant for a temporary change who is aggrieved by a denial of the Director for a temporary change pursuant to this order and the provisions of section 42-222A, Idaho Code, may request a hearing pursuant to section 42- 1701A(3), Idaho Code, and may seek judicial review of the final order of the Director pursuant to the provisions of section 42-1701A(4), Idaho Code. IT IS FURTHER HEREBY ORDERED that this order is effective upon approval of the ORDER-Pg2 Governor and expires on December 31, 2012, unless extended or terminated by order of the Director. Specifically, the Oxford Spring Snotel site, located in the eastern part of the county near Malad City and within the Malad River drainage, showed that year to date Snow Water Equivalent (SWE) was only 66 percent of average and the snow pack melted out about a month early; and WHEREAS, there are little or no storage facilities within Oneida County and many water users rely almost solely on natural stream flow supplies, and given the below normal precipitation levels within Oneida County, water supplies are limited; and WHEREAS, the United States Drought Monitor Index shows Oneida County included within that potion of Southeastern Idaho classified as moderate drought; and WHEREAS, section 42-222A, Idaho Code, provides that upon declaration of a drought emergency for an area designated by the Director of the Department of Water Resources ("Director") and approved by the Governor, the Director is authorized to allow temporary changes in the point of diversion, the place of use, and the purpose of use for valid existing water rights and temporary exchanges of water rights when the Director determines that such changes can be accomplished in accordance with the provisions of section 42-222A, Idaho Code; and NOW, THEREFORE, IT IS HEREBY ORDERED that pursuant to the authority of the Director provided in section 42-222A, Idaho Code, a drought emergency for purposes of section 42-222A, Idaho Code, is hereby declared for Oneida County, Idaho. IT IS FURTHER HEREBY ORDERED that pursuant to this declared drought emergency and the provisions of section 42-222A, Idaho Code, the following procedures and requirements shall apply to the filing, processing, and approval of any application for a temporary change to an ORDER-Pgl existing water right within Oneida County during the pendency of this declared drought emergency: 1. An application for a temporary change to an existing water right shall be made upon forms provided by the department and shall be accompanied by an application fee of fifty dollars ($50.00) per application. 2. The Director is not required to publish notice of the proposed change pursuant to the provisions of section 42-211, 42-222(1) or 42-240, Idaho Code, and is not required to make findings as provided in said sections. A temporary change may be approved upon completion of the application form, payment of the filing fee, and a determination by the Director that the proposed change can be properly administered and there is no information that the change will injure any other water right. If the right to be changed is administered by a watermaster within a water district, the Director shall obtain and consider the recommendations of the watermaster before approving the temporary change application. 3. All temporary changes approved pursuant to the provisions of this order shall expire on the date shown in the approval which shall not be later than December 31, 2013, and thereafter, the water right shall revert to the point of diversion and place of use existing prior to the temporary change. Nothing herein shall be construed as approval to authorize construction of a new well as a new point of diversion or to alter a stream channel. 4. The recipient of an approved temporary change issued pursuant to this order shall assume all risk of curtailment or mitigation should the diversion and use of water under the temporary change cause injury to other water rights or result in an enlargement in use of the original right. 5. Temporary changes shall only be approved for the purpose of providing a replacement water supply to lands or other uses that normally have a full water supply, except for the drought condition. Temporary changes may not be approved to provide water for new development or to allow expansion of the use of water under existing water rights. If the right to use the water is represented by shares of stock in a corporation, or if the diversion works or delivery system for such right is owned or managed by an irrigation district, no change in point of diversion, place or nature of use of such water shall be made or allowed without the written consent of such corporation or irrigation district. 6. Any applicant for a temporary change who is aggrieved by a denial of the Director for a temporary change pursuant to this order and the provisions of section 42-222A, Idaho Code, may request a hearing pursuant to section 42- 1701A(3), Idaho Code, and may seek judicial review of the final order of the Director pursuant to the provisions of section 42-1701A(4), Idaho Code. ORDER-Pg2 IT IS FURTHER HEREBY ORDERED that this order is effective upon approval of the Governor and expires on December 31, 2013, unless extended or terminated by order of the Director. full_text: BEFORE THE DEPARTMENT OF WATER RESOURCES OF THE STATE OF IDAHO IN THE MATTER OF A DECLARATION ) OF DROUGHT EMERGENCY FOR ) CLARK COUNTY ) ORDER DECLARING DROUGHT EMERGENCY WHEREAS, the Board of County Commissioners for Clark County has requested that the Governor and the Director of the Idaho Department of Water Resources declare a drought emergency for Clark County to allow administrative actions to lessen the severe impacts of drought conditions in the county; and WHEREAS, Clark County is included within the Camas Creek, Beaver Creek, Medicine Lodge Creek drainages and a portion of the Birch Creek drainage; and WHEREAS, snow water equivalent (SWE) levels for the Birch Creek drainage are normal or slightly above normal, SWE levels for the Camas, Beaver and Medicine Lodge drainages have been between 62 and 72 percent of normal during April, 2014, and stream flow volumes in the area for the period April through July are forecasted to be about 50 percent of average; and WHEREAS, the United States Drought Monitor Index shows Clark County classified as moderate to severe drought; and WHEREAS, there are little or no water storage facilities within Clark County and water users rely almost solely on natural stream flow supplies, and given that the drier than normal conditions within Clark County may result in tighter water supplies; and WHEREAS, section 42-222A, Idaho Code, provides that upon declaration of a drought emergency for an area designated by the Director of the Department of Water Resources ("Director") and approved by the Governor, the Director is authorized to allow temporary changes in the point of diversion, the place of use, and the purpose of use for valid existing water rights and temporary exchanges of water rights when the Director determines that such changes can be accomplished in accordance with the provisions of section 42-222A, Idaho Code; and NOW, THEREFORE, IT IS HEREBY ORDERED that pursuant to the authority of the Director provided in section 42-222A, Idaho Code, a drought emergency for purposes of section 42-222A, Idaho Code, is hereby declared for Clark County, Idaho. IT IS FURTHER HEREBY ORDERED that pursuant to this declared drought emergency and the provisions of section 42-222A, Idaho Code, the following procedures and requirements shall apply to the filing, processing, and approval of any application for a temporary change to an ORDER-Pg 1 existing water right within Clark County during the pendency of this declared drought emergency: 1. An application for a temporary change to an existing water right shall be made upon forms provided by the department and shall be accompanied by an application fee of fifty dollars ($50.00) per application. 2. The Director is not required to publish notice of the proposed change pursuant to the provisions of section 42-211, 42-222(1) or 42-240, Idaho Code, and is not required to make findings as provided in said sections. A temporary change may be approved upon completion of the application form, payment of the filing fee, and a determination by the Director that the proposed change can be properly administered and there is no information that the change will injure any other water right. If the right to be changed is administered by a watermaster within a water district, the Director shall obtain and consider the recommendations of the watermaster before approving the temporary change application. 3. All temporary changes approved pursuant to the provisions of this order shall expire on the date shown in the approval which shall not be later than December 31, 2014, and thereafter, the water right shall revert to the point of diversion and place of use existing prior to the temporary change. Nothing herein shall be construed as approval to authorize construction of a new well as a new point of diversion or to alter a stream channel. 4. The recipient of an approved temporary change issued pursuant to this order shall assume all risk of curtailment or mitigation should the diversion and use of water under the temporary change cause injury to other water rights or result in an enlargement in use of the original right. 5. Temporary changes shall only be approved for the purpose of providing a replacement water supply to lands or other uses that normally have a full water supply, except for the drought condition. Temporary changes may not be approved to provide water for new development or to allow expansion of the use of water under existing water rights. If the right to use the water is represented by shares of stock in a corporation, or if the diversion works or delivery system for such right is owned or managed by an irrigation district, no change in point of diversion, place or nature of use of such water shall be made or allowed without the written consent of such corporation or irrigation district. 6. Any applicant for a temporary change who is aggrieved by a denial of the Director for a temporary change pursuant to this order and the provisions of section 42-222A, Idaho Code, may request a hearing pursuant to section 42- 1701A(3), Idaho Code, and may seek judicial review of the final order of the Director pursuant to the provisions of section 42-1701A(4), Idaho Code. ORDER-Pg2 IT IS FURTHER HEREBY ORDERED that this order is effective upon approval of the Governor and expires on December 31, 2014 , unless extended or terminated by order of the Director. full_text: BEFORE THE DEPARTMENT OF WATER RESOURCES OF THE STATE OF IDAHO IN THE MATTER OF A DECLARATION ) OF DROUGHT EMERGENCY FOR ) FREMONT COUNTY ) ORDER DECLARING DROUGHT EMERGENCY WHEREAS, the Board of County Commissioners for Fremont County has requested that the Governor and the Director of the Idaho Department of Water Resources declare a drought emergency for Fremont County to allow administrative actions to lessen the impacts of drought conditions in the county; and WHEREAS, Fremont County is included within the Henrys Fork drainage basin, including the Falls River drainage; and WHEREAS, drainages in and around Fremont County are experiencing abnormally dry conditions due to below normal snowpack and precipitation levels. Specifically, total cumulative snow water equivalent levels in the Henry's Fork Basin above St. Anthony as of April 14, 2015 was 68 percent of normal while year to date precipitation was 70 percent of average. Stream flow volumes for the period April through September are forecasted to be only 60 percent of average for the Henrys Fork at Ashton and 68 percent of average for the Falls River near Ashton; and WHEREAS, the United States Drought Monitor Index on April 7, 2015, showed Fremont County included within that potion of Southern Idaho classified as abnormally dry to moderate drought; and WHEREAS, section 42-222A, Idaho Code, provides that upon declaration of a drought emergency for an area designated by the Director of the Department of Water Resources ("Director") and approved by the Governor, the Director is authorized to allow temporary changes in the point of di version, the place of use, and the purpose of use for valid existing water rights and temporary exchanges of water rights when the Director determines that such changes can be accomplished in accordance with the provisions of section 42-222A, Idaho Code; and NOW, THEREFORE, IT IS HEREBY ORDERED that pursuant to the authority of the Director provided in section 42-222A, Idaho Code, a drought emergency for purposes of section 42-222A, Idaho Code, is hereby declared for Fremont County, Idaho. IT IS FURTHER HEREBY ORDERED that pursuant to this declared drought emergency and the provisions of section 42-222A, Idaho Code, the following procedures and requirements shall apply to the filing, processing, and approval of any application for a temporary change to an existing water right within Fremont County during the pendency of this declared drought emergency: ORDER-Pg 1 1. An application for a temporary change to an existing water right shall be made upon forms provided by the department and shall be accompanied by an application fee of fifty dollars ($50.00) per application. 2. The Director is not required to publish notice of the proposed change pursuant to the provisions of section 42-211, 42-222(1) or 42-240, Idaho Code, and is not required to make findings as provided in said sections. A temporary change may be approved upon completion of the application form, payment of the filing fee, and a determination by the Director that the proposed change can be properly administered and there is no information that the change will injure any other water right. If the right to be changed is administered by a watermaster within a water district, the Director shall obtain and consider the recommendations of the watermaster before approving the temporary change application. 3. All temporary changes approved pursuant to the provisions of this order shall expire on the date shown in the approval which shall not be later than December 31, 2015, and thereafter, the water right shall revert to the point of di version and place of use existing prior to the temporary change. Nothing herein shall be construed as approval to authorize construction of a new well as a new point of diversion or to alter a stream channel. 4. The recipient of an approved temporary change issued pursuant to this order shall assume all risk of curtailment or mitigation should the diversion and use of water under the temporary change cause injury to other water rights or result in an enlargement in use of the original right. 5. Temporary changes shall only be approved for the purpose of providing a replacement water supply to lands or other uses that normally have a full water supply, except for the drought condition. Temporary changes may not be approved to provide water for new development or to allow expansion of the use of water under existing water rights. If the right to use the water is represented by shares of stock in a corporation, or if the diversion works or delivery system for such right is owned or managed by an irrigation district, no change in point of diversion, place or nature of use of such water shall be made or allowed without the written consent of such corporation or irrigation district. 6. Any applicant for a temporary change who is aggrieved by a denial of the Director for a temporary change pursuant to this order and the provisions of section 42-222A, Idaho Code, may request a hearing pursuant to section 42- 1701A(3), Idaho Code, and may seek judicial review of the final order of the Director pursuant to the provisions of section 42-1701A(4), Idaho Code. WHEREAS, Idaho Code §31-801 grants general powers and duties, subject to the restrictions of law, to the boards of county commissioners in their respective counties; and WHEREAS, Idaho Code §31-828 grants the board of commissioners authority "to do and perform all other acts ... which may be necessary to the full discharge of the duties of the chief executive authority of the county government."; and WHEREAS, Idaho Code §42-222A authorizes the Director of the Department of Water Resources, following the declaration of a drought emergency for an area designated by the Director and approved by the Governor, to allow temporary changes of point of diversion, place and purpose of use of valid existing water rights, so long as said changes will not injure existing water rights; and WHEREAS, Idaho Code §46-1011 provides that the Chairman of the Board of County Commissioners may declare a local disaster emergency, which may be continued in excess of seven days with consent of the Board of County Commissioners; and WHEREAS, Idaho Code §46-1002(3) provides, in part, that a "disaster" includes the imminent threat of widespread or severe damage or loss of property resulting from any natural or manmade cause; and WHEREAS, Idaho Code §46-1002(4) provides, in part, that an "emergency" includes the imminent threat of a "disaster" or condition threatening property which requires state emergency assistance to supplement local efforts to protect property or to avert or lessen the threat of "disaster."; and WHEREAS, based upon inquiry and preliminary discussions, water storage appears to be well below normal, historic levels and runoff appears to be well below normal, historic levels; and WHEREAS, the Board finds that the current low water levels pose an imminent threat of disaster to agriculture in Fremont County, which constitutes an emergency as defined in Idaho Code §46-1002(4);
